picks.rationale: Google is setting hard RAM budgets for Android apps from February 2027, so memory weight becomes a design constraint teams have to plan for now.
picks.excerpt: Facing a global RAM shortage tied to AI demand, Google sets new memory thresholds for Android apps starting February 2027, with penalties for non-compliance.

picks.rationale: Meta closes the capture-LED loophole and buys ads to teach people what the light means — privacy handled as industrial design plus signage, not a settings toggle.
picks.excerpt: Meta's smart glasses marketing campaign aims to spread 'awareness' about its LED capture light.

picks.rationale: Plaud rebuilds headphones around always-on note capture, a concrete answer to what an AI-first audio wearable should physically be.
picks.excerpt: The new AI device will be on display at IFA in Berlin next week.

picks.rationale: Hugging Face and Pollen put lidar, NFC and a programmable personality into a $399 open robot — cheap enough to make embodied AI an actual prototyping platform.
picks.excerpt: Microduck is Pollen Robotics' new programmable robot

picks.rationale: Whoop hides its sensor stack inside titanium Milanese mesh, a clear case of jewelry framing being used to make a sensor you never take off.
picks.excerpt: The titanium Milanese mesh hides Whoop's sensors in something that looks like jewelry, giving you even more reasons to never take them off.
